Self.Wiki: This map object represents an environmental map point in the map (vanilla: Env_PointNNN). Env Map Effect Boxes use the point whose three-digit suffix matches their env map number.

UnkMapID.Wiki: The map the point belongs to (formerly Unk18). In Elden Ring bytes 0-2 are compared with a map ID's AA/BB/CC; byte 0 = 0 means none. Byte 3 is not read. Retail Nightreign uses [0,0,0,2], or open-field tiles such as [60,8,8,2].

Unk00.Wiki: Unknown number. 1 on many points, else 0.5 to 1000 (8 is common). Not traced in the game.

Unk04.Wiki: Unknown. 4 on all but two points (2, 6). Not traced in the game.

Unk08.Wiki: Unknown. -1 on every point. Not traced in the game.

Unk0D.Wiki: Unknown. ON for most points. Not traced in the game.

Unk0E.Wiki: Unknown. ON for all but 9 points. Not traced in the game.

Unk0F.Wiki: Unknown. ON for all but 10 points. Not traced in the game.

Unk10.Wiki: Unknown number. 1 on every point. Not traced in the game.

Unk14.Wiki: Unknown number. 1 on every point. Not traced in the game.

Unk20.Wiki: Unknown; possibly a capture size. 512 on all but one point (256). Not traced in the game.

Unk24.Wiki: Unknown; possibly a capture size. 64 on most points, else 128 or 256. Not traced in the game.

Unk28.Wiki: Unknown. 5 on most points, else 6 or 7. Not traced in the game.

Unk2C.Wiki: Unknown. 0 on all but one point. Not traced in the game.

Unk2D.Wiki: Unknown. 2 or 1 on most points. Not traced in the game.
